classes.label: independent continuant
classes.definition: b is an independent continuant = Def. b is a continuant which is such that there is no c and no t such that b s-depends_on c at t. (axiom label in BFO2 Reference: [017-002])

classes.label: process
classes.definition: p is a process = Def. p is an occurrent that has temporal proper parts and for some time t, p s-depends_on some material entity at t. (axiom label in BFO2 Reference: [083-003])

classes.label: specifically dependent continuant
classes.definition: b is a specifically dependent continuant = Def. b is a continuant & there is some independent continuant c which is not a spatial region and which is such that b s-depends_on c at every time t during the course of b’s existence. (axiom label in BFO2 Reference: [050-003])

classes.label: generically dependent continuant
classes.definition: b is a generically dependent continuant = Def. b is a continuant that g-depends_on one or more other entities. (axiom label in BFO2 Reference: [074-001])

classes.label: process boundary
classes.definition: p is a process boundary =Def. p is a temporal part of a process & p has no proper temporal parts. (axiom label in BFO2 Reference: [084-001])

classes.label: continuant fiat boundary
classes.definition: b is a continuant fiat boundary = Def. b is an immaterial entity that is of zero, one or two dimensions and does not include a spatial region as part. (axiom label in BFO2 Reference: [029-001])

classes.label: process profile
classes.definition: b is a process_profile =Def. there is some process c such that b process_profile_of c (axiom label in BFO2 Reference: [093-002])

classes.label: relational quality
classes.definition: b is a relational quality = Def. for some independent continuants c, d and for some time t: b quality_of c at t & b quality_of d at t. (axiom label in BFO2 Reference: [057-001])

classes.label: conditioned taste aversion
classes.definition: A conditioned aversion to a specific chemical compound as a result of that compound being coupled with a noxious stimulus.

classes.label: behavioral fear response
classes.definition: An acute behavioral change resulting from a perceived external threat.

classes.label: suckling behavior
classes.definition: Specific behavior of a newborn or infant mammal that results in the derivation of nourishment from the breast.

classes.label: reduction of food intake in response to dietary excess
classes.definition: An eating behavior process whereby detection of a dietary excess results in a decrease in intake of nutrients.

classes.label: aggressive behavior
classes.definition: A behavioral interaction between organisms in which one organism has the intention of inflicting physical damage on another individual.

classes.label: predatory behavior
classes.definition: Aggressive behavior involving attack on prey by a predator.

classes.label: inter-male aggressive behavior
classes.definition: Aggressive behavior based on competition between males of the same species over access to resources such as females, dominance, status, etc. and characterized by noise, threats, and is often less injurious.

classes.label: fear-induced aggressive behavior
classes.definition: Aggressive behavior associated with attempts to flee from a threat.

classes.label: irritable aggressive behavior
classes.definition: Aggressive behavior induced by frustration and directed against an available target.

classes.label: territorial aggressive behavior
classes.definition: Aggressive behavior performed in defence of a fixed area against intruders, typically conspecifics.

classes.label: maternal aggressive behavior
classes.definition: Aggressive behavior of a female to protect her offspring from a threat.

classes.label: instrumental aggressive behavior
classes.definition: Aggressive behavior directed towards obtaining some goal, considered to be a learned response to a situation.

classes.label: behavioral defense response
classes.definition: A behavioral response seeking to protect an organism from an a perceived external threat to that organism.

classes.label: behavioral response to wounding
classes.definition: A behavioral response resulting from wounding.

classes.label: behavioral defense response to insect
classes.definition: A behavioral response seeking to protect an organism from an a perceived external threat from an insect or insects to that organism.

classes.label: behavioral defense response to nematode
classes.definition: A behavioral response seeking to protect an organism from an a perceived external threat from a nematode or nematodes to that organism.

classes.label: angiotensin-mediated drinking behavior
classes.definition: The drinking behavior that is mediated by the action of angiotensin in the brain. Angiotensin stimulates the brain centers that control thirst.

classes.label: behavior
classes.definition: The internally coordinated responses (actions or inactions) of animals (individuals or groups) to internal or external stimuli, via a mechanism that involves nervous system activity.

classes.label: learning or memory
classes.definition: The acquisition and processing of information and/or the storage and retrieval of this information over time.

classes.label: learning
classes.definition: Any process in an organism in which a relatively long-lasting adaptive behavioral change occurs as the result of experience.

classes.label: memory
classes.definition: The activities involved in the mental information processing system that receives (registers), modifies, stores, and retrieves informational stimuli. The main stages involved in the formation and retrieval of memory are encoding (processing of received information by acquisition), storage (building a permanent record of received information as a result of consolidation) and retrieval (calling back the stored information and use it in a suitable way to execute a given task).

classes.label: short-term memory
classes.definition: The memory process that deals with the storage, retrieval and modification of information received a short time (up to about 30 minutes) ago. This type of memory is typically dependent on direct, transient effects of second messenger activation.

classes.label: anesthesia-resistant memory
classes.definition: The memory process that results in the formation of consolidated memory resistant to disruption of the patterned activity of the brain, without requiring protein synthesis.

classes.label: long-term memory
classes.definition: The memory process that deals with the storage, retrieval and modification of information a long time (typically weeks, months or years) after receiving that information. This type of memory is typically dependent on gene transcription regulated by second messenger activation.

classes.label: mating behavior
classes.definition: The behavioral interactions between organisms for the purpose of mating, or sexual reproduction resulting in the formation of zygotes.

classes.label: courtship behavior
classes.definition: The behavioral interactions between organisms for the purpose of attracting sexual partners.

classes.label: negative regulation of female receptivity
classes.definition: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the receptiveness of a female to male advances.

classes.label: rhythmic behavior
classes.definition: The specific behavior of an organism that recur with measured regularity.

classes.label: grooming behavior
classes.definition: The specific behavior of an organism relating to grooming, cleaning and brushing to remove dirt and parasites.

classes.label: locomotory behavior
classes.definition: The specific movement from place to place of an organism in response to external or internal stimuli. Locomotion of a whole organism in a manner dependent upon some combination of that organism's internal state and external conditions.

classes.label: adult walking behavior
classes.definition: The behavior of an adult relating to the progression of that organism along the ground by the process of lifting and setting down each leg.

classes.label: flight behavior
classes.definition: The response to external or internal stimuli that results in the locomotory process of flight. Flight is the self-propelled movement of an organism through the air.

classes.label: jump response
classes.definition: The sudden, usually upward, movement off the ground or other surface through sudden muscular effort in the legs, following exposure to an external stimulus.

classes.label: feeding behavior
classes.definition: Behavior associated with the intake of food.

classes.label: visual behavior
classes.definition: The behavior of an organism in response to a visual stimulus.

classes.label: pattern orientation
classes.definition: The actions or reactions of an individual in response to the orientation of a visual pattern. This is exemplified by some classes of insects which are able to detect and learn the orientation of a set of stripes and subsequently behaviorally discriminate between horizontal, vertical or 45 degree stripes.

classes.label: optokinetic behavior
classes.definition: The behavior of an organism pertaining to movement of the eyes and of objects in the visual field, as in nystagmus.

classes.label: chemosensory behavior
classes.definition: Behavior that is dependent upon the sensation of chemicals.

classes.label: chemosensory jump behavior
classes.definition: The sudden, usually upward, movement off the ground or other surface through sudden muscular effort in the legs, following exposure to a chemical substance.

classes.label: proboscis extension reflex
classes.definition: The extension, through direct muscle actions, of the proboscis (the trunk-like extension of the mouthparts on the adult external head) in response to a sugar stimulus.

classes.label: mechanosensory behavior
classes.definition: Behavior that is dependent upon the sensation of a mechanical stimulus.

classes.label: male courtship behavior
classes.definition: The behavior of a male, for the purpose of attracting a sexual partner. An example of this process is found in Drosophila melanogaster.

classes.label: female courtship behavior
classes.definition: The behavior of a female, for the purpose of attracting a sexual partner.

classes.label: eclosion rhythm
classes.definition: The timing of the emergence of the adult fly from its pupal case, which usually occurs at dawn.

classes.label: associative learning
classes.definition: Learning by associating a stimulus (the cause) with a particular outcome (the effect).

classes.label: adult feeding behavior
classes.definition: Feeding behavior in a fully developed and mature organism.

classes.label: adult locomotory behavior
classes.definition: Locomotory behavior in a fully developed and mature organism.

classes.label: larval locomotory behavior
classes.definition: Locomotory behavior in a larval (immature) organism.

classes.label: larval walking behavior
classes.definition: The behavior of a larval organism relating to the progression of that organism along the ground by the process of lifting and setting down each leg.

classes.label: olfactory learning
classes.definition: Any process in an organism in which a relatively long-lasting adaptive behavioral change occurs in response to (repeated) exposure to an olfactory cue.

classes.label: visual learning
classes.definition: Any process in an organism in which a change in behavior of an individual occurs in response to repeated exposure to a visual cue.

classes.label: male courtship behavior, orientation prior to leg tapping and wing vibration
classes.definition: The process during courtship, where the male orients towards a potential partner. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster.

classes.label: male courtship behavior, tapping to detect pheromone
classes.definition: The process during courtship where the male insect taps the female with his frontal leg. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster.

classes.label: male courtship behavior, veined wing vibration
classes.definition: The process during courtship where the male insect vibrates his wings. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster.
parent_labels: male courtship behavior, veined wing extension

classes.label: male courtship behavior, proboscis-mediated licking
classes.definition: The process during courtship where the male fly licks the genitalia of a stationary female fly with his proboscis. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster.

classes.label: oviposition
classes.definition: The deposition of eggs (either fertilized or not) upon a surface or into a medium such as water.

classes.label: reproductive behavior
classes.definition: The specific behavior of an organism that is associated with reproduction.

classes.label: circadian sleep/wake cycle process
classes.definition: A behavioral process involved in the cycle from wakefulness through an orderly succession of sleep states and stages that occurs on an approximately 24 hour rhythm.

classes.label: adult behavior
classes.definition: Behavior in a fully developed and mature organism.

classes.label: larval feeding behavior
classes.definition: Feeding behavior in a larval (immature) organism.

classes.label: larval behavior
classes.definition: Behavior in a larval form of an organism, an immature organism that must undergo metamorphosis to assume adult characteristics.

classes.label: auditory behavior
classes.definition: The behavior of an organism in response to a sound.

classes.label: host-seeking behavior
classes.definition: The specific behavior of an organism that are associated with finding a host organism; may include behavioral responses to light, temperature, or chemical emanations from the prospective host.

classes.label: response to hermaphrodite contact
classes.definition: The response by the male to a hermaphrodite after initial contact following mate finding. The male stops forward locomotion, presses the ventral side of his tail against his partner's body, and begins moving backward along the hermaphrodite. Male response behavior is initiated when sensory neurons located in the rays of his tail contact a potential mate.

classes.label: turning behavior involved in mating
classes.definition: The sharp ventral turn performed by the male as he approaches either the hermaphrodite head or tail, whilst trying to locate his partner's vulva. Turning occurs via a sharp ventral coil of the male's tail.

classes.label: vulval location
classes.definition: Location, by the male, of his partner's vulva when backing along the ventral side of the hermaphrodite during mating. The male stops at the vulva, coordinates his movements to the hermaphrodite's, and positions his tail precisely over the vulva so that he may insert his spicules and ejaculate.

classes.label: spicule insertion
classes.definition: Insertion of the male copulatory spicules into the hermaphrodite. Spicule insertion behavior initiates when the male cloaca contacts the vulva. During most mating encounters, the spicule tips will prod the vulva continuously until they partially penetrate, which then causes the protractors to contract completely so that the spicules extend through the vulva.

classes.label: behavioral response to nicotine
classes.definition: Any process that results in a change in the behavior of an organism as a result of a nicotine stimulus.

classes.label: operant conditioning
classes.definition: Learning to anticipate future events on the basis of past experience with the consequences of one's own behavior.

classes.label: social behavior
classes.definition: Behavior directed towards society, or taking place between members of the same species. Occurs predominantly, or only, in individuals that are part of a group.

classes.label: larval foraging behavior
classes.definition: The movement of a larva through a feeding substrate whilst feeding on food.

classes.label: turning behavior
classes.definition: Fine-tuning the spatial position of an organism in response to variability in their environment. For example, reorientation of an organism in the direction of a food source.

classes.label: larval turning behavior
classes.definition: Fine-tuning the spatial position of a larva in response to variability in their environment. For example, reorientation of a larva in the direction of a food source.

classes.label: larval wandering behavior
classes.definition: The movement of a third instar larva through a substrate in search of a pupation site. This movement occurs without feeding and is characterized by short bursts of forward movement, separated by stops and repeated side-to-side head probes, followed normally by a change in direction.

classes.label: larval burrowing behavior
classes.definition: Digging into the substrate by non-feeding larvae in search for food-free sites suitable for pupation.

classes.label: hatching behavior
classes.definition: The specific behavior of an organism during the emergence from an egg shell. In Drosophila for example, the larva swings its head reiteratively through a semicircular arc, using its mouth hooks to tear apart the chorion in front of it and thus free itself from within the egg shell.

classes.label: salt aversion
classes.definition: The specific avoidance actions or reactions of an organism in response to the perception of salt.

classes.label: exploration behavior
classes.definition: The specific behavior of an organism in response to a novel environment or stimulus.

classes.label: locomotory exploration behavior
classes.definition: The specific movement from place to place of an organism in response to a novel environment.

classes.label: circadian mating behavior
classes.definition: The fluctuation in mating behavior that occurs over an approximately 24 hour cycle.

classes.label: injection of substance in to other organism
classes.definition: The process of forcing a substance into another organism, either by penetrating the skin of the other organism or by applying the substance externally to a sensitive tissue such as those that surround the eyes.

classes.label: envenomation resulting in modification of morphology or physiology of other organism
classes.definition: The process which begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the manifestation of some change or damage to the bitten organism.
parent_labels: injection of substance in to other organism

classes.label: swimming behavior
classes.definition: The response to external or internal stimuli that results in the locomotory process of swimming. Swimming is the self-propelled movement of an organism through the water.

classes.label: psychomotor behavior
classes.definition: The specific behavior of an organism that combines cognitive functions and physical movement. For example, driving a car, throwing a ball, or playing a musical instrument.

classes.label: thermosensory behavior
classes.definition: Behavior that is dependent upon the sensation of temperature.

classes.label: olfactory behavior
classes.definition: The behavior of an organism in response to an odor.

classes.label: vocal learning
classes.definition: A behavioral process whose outcome is a relatively long-lasting behavioral change whereby an organism modifies innate vocalizations to imitate sounds produced by others.
parent_labels: learned vocalization behavior or vocal learning

classes.label: mating plug formation
classes.definition: The deposition of a plug of sperm or other gelatinous material into the opening of the vulva by a male at the termination of copulation. Probably acts to prevent subsequent matings by other males.

classes.label: behavioral response to water deprivation
classes.definition: Any process that results in a change in the behavior of an organism as a result of deprivation of water.

classes.label: maternal behavior
classes.definition: Female behaviors associated with the care and rearing of offspring.

classes.label: paternal behavior
classes.definition: Male behaviors associated with the care and rearing offspring.

classes.label: circadian sleep/wake cycle
classes.definition: The cycle from wakefulness through an orderly succession of sleep states and stages that occurs on an approximately 24 hour rhythm.

classes.label: circadian sleep/wake cycle, wakefulness
classes.definition: The part of the circadian sleep/wake cycle where the organism is not asleep.

classes.label: circadian sleep/wake cycle, REM sleep
classes.definition: A stage in the circadian sleep cycle during which dreams occur and the body undergoes marked changes including rapid eye movement, loss of reflexes, and increased pulse rate and brain activity.

classes.label: circadian sleep/wake cycle, non-REM sleep
classes.definition: All sleep stages in the circadian sleep/wake cycle other than REM sleep. These stages are characterized by a slowing of brain waves and other physiological functions.

classes.label: eating behavior
classes.definition: The specific behavior of an organism relating to the intake of food, any substance (usually solid) that can be metabolized by an organism to give energy and build tissue.

classes.label: drinking behavior
classes.definition: The specific behavior of an organism relating to the intake of liquids, especially water.

classes.label: pharyngeal pumping
classes.definition: The contraction and relaxation movements of the pharyngeal muscle that mediate feeding in nematodes.

classes.label: envenomation resulting in hemorrhagic damage to other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with vascular damage and hemorrhage in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modification of morphology or physiology of other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in modulation of platelet aggregation in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with a resultant change to the frequency, rate or extent of platelet aggregation in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modulation of blood coagulation in other organism

classes.label: injection of substance into other organism during feeding on blood of other organism
classes.definition: The process of forcing a substance into the bloodstream of another organism, whilst feeding on blood of other organism. The substance may facilitate the feeding process, e.g. by preventing the blood from clotting.
parent_labels: injection of substance in to other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in induction of edema in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the swelling of soft tissues of the bitten organism as a result of excess water accumulation.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modification of morphology or physiology of other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in modulation of blood coagulation in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the modulation of the frequency, rate or extent of blood coagulation in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modification of morphology or physiology of other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in positive regulation of blood coagulation in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the resultant activation, maintenance or an increase in the frequency, rate or extent of blood coagulation in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modulation of blood coagulation in other organism

parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modulation of blood coagulation in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in pore formation in membrane of other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a pore complex in a membrane of the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modification of morphology or physiology of other organism

classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the resultant modulation of blood mast cell degranulation in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modification of morphology or physiology of other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in positive regulation of mast cell degranulation in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the resultant positive regulation of blood mast cell degranulation in the bitten organism.

classes.label: envenomation resulting in proteolysis in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the resultant hydrolysis of proteins in of the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modification of morphology or physiology of other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in blood vessel extracellular matrix damage, causing hemorrhagic damage in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism which causes damage to the extracellular matrix of the blood vessels of the bitten organism, ultimately resulting in hemorrhage in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in hemorrhagic damage to other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in impairment of hemostasis in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the inhibition of the process of hemostasis - the stopping of bleeding or the arrest of the circulation to an organ or part - in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modification of morphology or physiology of other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in fibrinolysis in other organism
classes.definition: The process which begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with fibrinolysis, a process that solubilizes fibrin, chiefly by the proteolytic action of plasmin, in the bloodstream of the bitten/stung organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in impairment of hemostasis in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in fibrinogenolysis in other organism
classes.definition: The process which begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with fibrinogenolysis, a process that degrades fibrinogen at a variety of Arg-Lys bonds, thus impairing fibrinogen clotting in the bloodstream of the bitten/stung organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in depletion of circulating fibrinogen in other organism

classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the resultant modulation of the transmission of nerve impulses in the bitten organism.

parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modulation of receptor activity in other organism

classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the resultant modulation of G-protein coupled receptor activity in of the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modulation of receptor activity in other organism

classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the resultant positive regulation of G-protein coupled receptor activity in of the bitten organism.

classes.label: envenomation resulting in modulation of vasoactive intestinal polypeptide receptor activity in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in positive regulation of vasoactive intestinal polypeptide receptor activity in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the resultant positive regulation of the activity of a vasoactive intestinal polypeptide receptor in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modulation of vasoactive intestinal polypeptide receptor activity in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in muscle damage in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with resultant muscle damage in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modification of morphology or physiology of other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in myocyte killing in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, killing heart myocytes and ultimately resulting in muscle damage in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in muscle damage in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in damage of muscle extracellular matrix in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, damaging the extracellular matrix of muscle cells and ultimately resulting in muscle necrosis in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in muscle damage in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in modulation of apoptotic process in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the resultant modulation of apoptosis in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modification of morphology or physiology of other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in depletion of circulating fibrinogen in other organism
classes.definition: The process which begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with a reduction in the quantity of fibrinogen found in the bloodstream of the bitten/stung organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in impairment of hemostasis in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in zymogen activation in other organism
classes.definition: The process which begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the proteolytic processing of an inactive enzyme to an active form.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modification of morphology or physiology of other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in plasminogen activation in other organism
classes.definition: The process which begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the activation of plasminogen into plasmin in the bitten organism. This process includes cleavage at an internal Arg-Val site to form an N-terminal A-chain and C-terminal B-chain held together by a disulfide bond, and can include further proteolytic cleavage events to remove the preactivation peptide.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in fibrinolysis in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in vasodilation in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with resultant vasodilation of blood vessels, usually causing a reduction in blood pressure, in the bitten/stung organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in negative regulation of blood pressure in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in negative regulation of heart rate of other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the negative regulation of the heart rate of the bitten/stung organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modification of morphology or physiology of other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in modulation of voltage-gated potassium channel activity in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with a resultant change in the activity of a voltage-gated potassium channel in the bitten/stung organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modulation of ion channel activity in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in modulation of ion channel activity in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with a resultant change in the activity of an ion channel in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modification of morphology or physiology of other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in negative regulation of voltage-gated potassium channel activity in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with a resultant negative regulation of the activity of a voltage-gated potassium channel in the bitten/stung organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modulation of voltage-gated potassium channel activity in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in slowing of activation kinetics of voltage-gated potassium channel in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with a resultant slowing of the activation kinetics of the activity of a voltage-gated potassium channel in the bitten/stung organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in negative regulation of voltage-gated potassium channel activity in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in occlusion of the pore of voltage-gated potassium channel in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with a resultant blocking of a voltage-gated potassium channel, inhibiting the pore's activity, in the bitten/stung organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in negative regulation of voltage-gated potassium channel activity in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in modulation of cell migration in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the modulation of cell migration in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modification of morphology or physiology of other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in negative regulation of cell migration in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the negative regulation of cell migration in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modulation of cell migration in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in positive regulation of cell migration in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the positive regulation of cell migration in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modulation of cell migration in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in modulation of complement activation, classical pathway in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the regulation of complement activation via the classical pathway of the bitten/stung organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modulation of complement activation in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in negative regulation of complement activation, classical pathway in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the negative regulation of complement activation via the classical pathway of the bitten/stung organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modulation of complement activation, classical pathway in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in positive regulation of complement activation, classical pathway in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the positive regulation of complement activation via the classical pathway of the bitten/stung organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modulation of complement activation, classical pathway in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in modulation of complement activation, lectin pathway in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the resultant modulation of complement activation via the lectin pathway in the bitten/stung organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modulation of complement activation in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in negative regulation of complement activation, lectin pathway in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the resultant negative regulation of complement activation via the lectin pathway in the bitten/stung organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modulation of complement activation, lectin pathway in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in positive regulation of complement activation, lectin pathway in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the resultant positive regulation of complement activation via the lectin pathway in the bitten/stung organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modulation of complement activation, lectin pathway in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in modulation of complement activation, alternative pathway in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the resultant modulation of complement activation via the alternative pathway in the bitten/stung organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modulation of complement activation in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in positive regulation of complement activation, alternative pathway in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the resultant positive regulation of complement activation via the alternative pathway in the bitten/stung organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modulation of complement activation, alternative pathway in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in negative regulation of complement activation, alternative pathway in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the resultant negative regulation of complement activation via the alternative pathway in the bitten/stung organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modulation of complement activation, alternative pathway in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in modulation of complement activation in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the resultant modulation of complement activation in the bitten/stung organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modification of morphology or physiology of other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in cytolysis in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with cytolysis in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modification of morphology or physiology of other organism

classes.label: multi-organism reproductive behavior
classes.definition: The specific behavior of an organism that is associated with reproduction involving another organism of the same or different species.

classes.label: envenomation resulting in modulation of acid-sensing ion channel activity in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with a resultant change in the activity of an acid-sensing ion channel (ASIC) in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modulation of ion channel activity in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in positive regulation of acid-sensing ion channel activity in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with a resultant positive regulation in the activity of an acid-sensing ion channel (ASIC) in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modulation of acid-sensing ion channel activity in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in negative regulation of acid-sensing ion channel activity in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with a resultant negative regulation in the activity of an acid-sensing ion channel (ASIC) in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modulation of acid-sensing ion channel activity in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in negative regulation of sensory perception of pain in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the inhibition of the sensory perception of pain in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modulation of sensory perception of pain in other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in modulation of sensory perception of pain in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the modulation of the sensory perception of pain in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modification of morphology or physiology of other organism

classes.label: post-mating behavior
classes.definition: The specific behavior of an organism following mating.

classes.label: male courtship behavior, veined wing generated song production
classes.definition: The process during wing vibration where the male insect produces a species-specific acoustic signal called a love song.

classes.label: negative regulation of female receptivity, post-mating
classes.definition: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the receptiveness of a female to male advances subsequent to mating.

classes.label: locomotor rhythm
classes.definition: The rhythm of the locomotor activity of an organism during its 24 hour activity cycle.

classes.label: regulation of female receptivity
classes.definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the willingness or readiness of a female to receive male advances.

classes.label: positive regulation of female receptivity
classes.definition: Any process that activates or increases the receptiveness of a female to male advances.

classes.label: regulation of female receptivity, post-mating
classes.definition: Any process that modulates the receptiveness of a female to male advances subsequent to mating.

classes.label: positive regulation of female receptivity, post-mating
classes.definition: Any process that increases the receptiveness of a female to male advances subsequent to mating.

classes.label: nonassociative learning
classes.definition: A simple form of learning whereby the repeated presence of a stimulus leads to a change in the probability or strength of the response to that stimulus. There is no association of one type of stimulus with another, rather it is a generalized response to the environment.

classes.label: habituation
classes.definition: A decrease in a behavioral response to a repeated stimulus. This is exemplified by the failure of a person to show a startle response to a loud noise that has been repeatedly presented.

classes.label: sensitization
classes.definition: An increased in a behavioral response to a repeated stimulus. For example, a shock to the tail of the marine snail Aplysia, to which the snail responds by withdrawing its gill, will result in increased gill withdrawal the next time the skin is touched.

classes.label: mating behavior, sex discrimination
classes.definition: The behavior of individuals for the purpose of discriminating between the sexes, for the purpose of finding a suitable mating partner.

classes.label: male courtship behavior, veined wing extension
classes.definition: The process during courtship where the male insect extends his wings. An example of this process is found in Drosophila melanogaster.

classes.label: behavioral response to cocaine
classes.definition: Any process that results in a change in the behavior of an organism as a result of a cocaine stimulus.

classes.label: behavioral response to ethanol
classes.definition: Any process that results in a change in the behavior of an organism as a result of an ethanol stimulus.

classes.label: behavioral response to ether
classes.definition: Any process that results in a change in the behavior of an organism as a result of an ether stimulus.

classes.label: behavioral response to pain
classes.definition: Any process that results in a change in the behavior of an organism as a result of a pain stimulus. Pain stimuli cause activation of nociceptors, peripheral receptors for pain, include receptors which are sensitive to painful mechanical stimuli, extreme heat or cold, and chemical stimuli.

classes.label: circadian behavior
classes.definition: The specific behavior of an organism that recurs with a regularity of approximately 24 hours.

classes.label: circadian sleep/wake cycle, sleep
classes.definition: The part of the circadian sleep/wake cycle where the organism is asleep.

classes.label: multi-organism behavior
classes.definition: Any process in which an organism has a behavioral effect on another organism of the same or different species.

classes.label: behavioral response to nutrient
classes.definition: Any process that results in a change in the behavior of an organism as a result of a nutrient stimulus.

classes.label: general adaptation syndrome, behavioral process
classes.definition: The set of behavioral processes that occur as part of the general adaptation syndrome, the response of the body to a strong, stressful stimulus.

classes.label: male mating behavior
classes.definition: The specific behavior of a male organism that is associated with reproduction.

classes.label: female mating behavior
classes.definition: The specific behavior of a female organism that is associated with reproduction.

classes.label: crying behavior
classes.definition: The behavior in which an organism sheds tears, often accompanied by non-verbal vocalizations and in response to external or internal stimuli.

classes.label: post-mating oviposition
classes.definition: The deposition of eggs, either fertilized or not, upon a surface or into a medium, following mating.

classes.label: parental behavior
classes.definition: A reproductive behavior in which a parent cares for and rears offspring.

classes.label: oral incubation
classes.definition: A parental behavior in which fertilized eggs are taken into the mouth and held until hatching.

classes.label: foraging behavior
classes.definition: Behavior by which an organism locates food.

classes.label: adult foraging behavior
classes.definition: Behavior by which an adult locates food.

classes.label: foraging behavior by probing substrate
classes.definition: Foraging behavior in which an anatomical part of the organism is inserted into the substrate to locate food.

classes.label: behavioral response to chemical pain
classes.definition: Any process that results in a change in the behaviour of an organism as a result of a chemical pain stimulus.

classes.label: behavioral response to acetic acid induced pain
classes.definition: Any process that results in a change in the behaviour of an organism as a result of an acetic acid pain stimulus.

classes.label: behavioral response to formalin induced pain
classes.definition: Any process that results in a change in the behaviour of an organism as a result of a formalin pain stimulus.

classes.label: motor learning
classes.definition: Any process in which an organism acquires a novel neuromuscular action or movement as the result of experience.

classes.label: motor behavior
classes.definition: The specific neuromuscular movement of a single organism in response to external or internal stimuli.

classes.label: vocalization behavior
classes.definition: The behavior in which an organism produces sounds by a mechanism involving its respiratory system.

classes.label: optomotor response
classes.definition: Eye, head or whole body movements that help to compensate movements of the environment in order to stabilize its image on the retina. In the case of whole body movements, these motor actions may also stabilize a locomotor course in response to some disturbance. Examples include: the optokinetic reflex, which allows human eyes to follow objects in motion while the head remains stationary reflex; the optomotor responses of flying insects and swimming fish.

classes.label: medium-term memory
classes.definition: The memory process that deals with the storage, retrieval and modification of information received at a time ago that is intermediate between that of short and long term memory (30min - 7hrs in Drosophila melanogaster).

classes.label: walking behavior
classes.definition: The behavior of an organism relating to the progression of that organism along the ground by the process of lifting and setting down each leg.

classes.label: dishabituation
classes.definition: The temporary recovery of response to a stimulus when a novel stimulus is added.

classes.label: innate vocalization behavior
classes.definition: A vocalisation behavior that is innate, i.e. that does not need to be learned in order to occur.

classes.label: learned vocalization behavior
classes.definition: A vocalization behavior that is the result of learning.
parent_labels: learned vocalization behavior or vocal learning

classes.label: imitative learning
classes.definition: Learning in which new behaviors are acquired through imitation.

classes.label: observational learning
classes.definition: Learning that occurs through observing the behavior of others.

classes.label: learned vocalization behavior or vocal learning
classes.definition: Vocalisation behavior that is the result of learning, or the process by which new vocalizations are learned.

classes.label: envenomation resulting in positive regulation of argininosuccinate synthase activity in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with the activation of the cytosolic argininosuccinate synthase in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in modification of morphology or physiology of other organism

classes.label: envenomation resulting in hemolysis in other organism
classes.definition: A process that begins with venom being forced into an organism by the bite or sting of another organism, and ends with hemolysis in the bitten organism.
parent_labels: envenomation resulting in cytolysis in other organism

classes.label: conditioned place preference
classes.definition: The associative learning process by which an animal learns and remembers an association between a neutral, unchanging environment and a putatively rewarding, internal state produced by a xenobiotic or drug.

classes.label: curation status specification
classes.definition: The curation status of the term. The allowed values come from an enumerated list of predefined terms. See the specification of these instances for more detailed definitions of each enumerated value.

classes.label: data about an ontology part
classes.definition: Data about an ontology part is a data item about a part of an ontology, for example a term

classes.label: obsolescence reason specification
classes.definition: The reason for which a term has been deprecated. The allowed values come from an enumerated list of predefined terms. See the specification of these instances for more detailed definitions of each enumerated value.

classes.label: denotator type
classes.definition: A denotator type indicates how a term should be interpreted from an ontological perspective.

classes.label: base ontology module
classes.definition: An ontology module that comprises only of asserted axioms local to the ontology, excludes import directives, and excludes axioms or declarations from external ontologies.

classes.label: editors ontology module
classes.definition: An ontology module that is intended to be directly edited, typically managed in source control, and typically not intended for direct consumption by end-users.

classes.label: main release ontology module
classes.definition: An ontology module that is intended to be the primary release product and the one consumed by the majority of tools.

classes.label: bridge ontology module
classes.definition: An ontology module that consists entirely of axioms that connect or bridge two distinct ontology modules. For example, the Uberon-to-ZFA bridge module.

classes.label: import ontology module
classes.definition: A subset ontology module that is intended to be imported from another ontology.

classes.label: subset ontology module
classes.definition: An ontology module that is extracted from a main ontology module and includes only a subset of entities or axioms.

classes.label: curation subset ontology module
classes.definition: A subset ontology that is intended as a whitelist for curators using the ontology. Such a subset will exclude classes that curators should not use for curation.

classes.label: analysis subset ontology module
classes.definition: An ontology module that is intended for usage in analysis or discovery applications.

classes.label: single layer subset ontology module
classes.definition: A subset ontology that is largely comprised of a single layer or strata in an ontology class hierarchy. The purpose is typically for rolling up for visualization. The classes in the layer need not be disjoint.

classes.label: exclusion subset ontology module
classes.definition: A subset of an ontology that is intended to be excluded for some purpose. For example, a blacklist of classes.

classes.label: external import ontology module
classes.definition: An imported ontology module that is derived from an external ontology. Derivation methods include the OWLAPI SLME approach.

classes.label: species subset ontology module
classes.definition: A subset ontology that is crafted to either include or exclude a taxonomic grouping of species.

classes.label: reasoned ontology module
classes.definition: An ontology module that contains axioms generated by a reasoner. The generated axioms are typically direct SubClassOf axioms, but other possibilities are available.

classes.label: generated ontology module
classes.definition: An ontology module that is automatically generated, for example via a SPARQL query or via template and a CSV.

classes.label: template generated ontology module
classes.definition: An ontology module that is automatically generated from a template specification and fillers for slots in that template.

classes.label: obo basic subset ontology module
classes.definition:
A subset ontology that is designed for basic applications to continue to make certain simplifying assumptions; many of these simplifying assumptions were based on the initial version of the Gene Ontology, and have become enshrined in many popular and useful tools such as term enrichment tools.

Examples of such assumptions include: traversing the ontology graph ignoring relationship types using a naive algorithm will not lead to cycles (i.e. the ontology is a DAG); every referenced term is declared in the ontology (i.e. there are no dangling clauses).

An ontology is OBO Basic if and only if it has the following characteristics:
DAG
Unidirectional
No Dangling Clauses
Fully Asserted
Fully Labeled
No equivalence axioms
Singly labeled edges
No qualifier lists
No disjointness axioms
No owl-axioms header
No imports

classes.label: ontology module subsetted by OWL profile
EL++ ontology module
parent_labels: ontology module subsetted by OWL profile

classes.label: mental functioning related anatomical structure
classes.definition: An anatomical structure in which there inheres the disposition to be the agent of a mental process.

classes.label: disposition to be agent of mental process
remembering
classes.definition: (for the case of remembering X, where X is an event in the organism’s history) a mental process that is a) about X, and b) made possible by the physical traces left by a causal process involving the organism during the event X

classes.label: alertness
classes.definition:
State of active attention by high sensory awareness such as being watchful and prompt to meet danger or emergency, or being quick to perceive and act.

 http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alertness

classes.label: mental counting
classes.definition: A cognitive process that involves the mental representation of sequential numbers.

classes.label: mental calculation
classes.definition: A cognitive process that involves the manipulation of mental representations of numeric entities in order to compute the outcome of a mathematical function.

classes.label: judging
classes.definition: A mental process during which information is evaluated, the outcome of which is a belief or opinion.

classes.label: determining gender
classes.definition: A judging process during which an opinion about the gender of a person is determined.

classes.label: cognitive process
classes.definition: A mental process that creates, modifies or has as participant some cognitive representation.

classes.label: determining orientation
classes.definition: A judging that involves the determination of the orientation of some object.

classes.label: arousal
classes.definition: A mental process that is the psychological and physiological state of being awake and reactive to stimuli.

classes.label: thinking
classes.definition: a mental process that involves the manipulation of mental language and/or mental images

classes.label: imagination
classes.definition: A mental process that manipulates mental images and words that go beyond mere memory and thoughts about the objects and entities that the person has encountered, to visualise or consider entities and states of affairs that the person has never encountered and which may not yet exist or obtain in the world. Imagination is the capacity to produce images, ideas and sensations in the mind without any immediate input of the senses.

classes.label: human being
classes.definition: An extended organism that is a member of the species Homo sapiens.

classes.label: consciousness
classes.definition: Consciousness is an inseparable part of some mental processes. It is that part of the mental process that: a) confers a subjective perspective, a phenomenology, an experience of the mental process of which it is a part; and b) intends the object or event that the mental process is about, should such exist; i.e., it confers intentionality on the mental process.

classes.label: attending
classes.definition: the process whereby relevant aspects of our mental experience are focused on specific targets

classes.label: perception
classes.definition:
A mental process which is 
a) produced by a causal process involving a part of the environment of the organism, and 
b) is experienced by the organism as being so caused, and 
c) in which the relevant part of the environment is thereby represented to the organism.

classes.label: mental process
classes.definition: A bodily process that occurs in the brain, and that can of itself be conscious, or can give rise to a process that can of itself be conscious or can give rise to behaviour.

classes.label: interpersonal process
classes.definition: A bodily process in which at least two human beings are agents.

classes.label: agreeableness
classes.definition: A personality trait manifesting itself in individual behavioral characteristics that are perceived as kind, sympathetic, cooperative, warm, and considerate.

classes.label: interpersonal behavior
classes.definition: Behavior having interpersonal processes as parts, each involving the same instances of human being.

classes.label: seeing
classes.definition:
Seeing (visual perception) is a mental process that is
a) produced by a causal process involving light rays from a part of the environment of the subject being absorbed by photoreceptors in the retina, and
b) is experienced by the subject as being so caused, and
c) in which the relevant part of the environment is thereby represented to the subject

classes.label: intelligence
classes.definition: A mental capability realised in processes involving understanding complex ideas, adapting effectively to the environment, learning from experience, engaging in various forms of reasoning, and overcome obstacles through the outcome of thinking processes.

classes.label: planning
classes.definition: A mental process that involves mentally manipulating representations of steps in an imagined process which has some goal.

classes.label: conscientiousness
classes.definition: A personality trait manifesting itself in individual behavioral characteristics that are perceived as careful, self-disciplined, dependable, vigilant, dutiful, and goal-oriented.

classes.label: irascibility
classes.definition: A mental disposition to frequent or easily incited outbursts of anger.

classes.label: representation
classes.definition: A dependent continuant which is about a portion of reality.

classes.label: cognitive representation
classes.definition: A representation which specifically depends on an anatomical structure in the cognitive system of an organism.

classes.label: bodily disposition
classes.definition: A bodily disposition is a disposition that inheres in some extended organism. Examples are: my disposition to catch a cold when exposed to a virus, my ability to speak the English language.

classes.label: mental disposition
classes.definition: A mental disposition is a bodily disposition that is realized in a mental process.

classes.label: visual consciousness
classes.definition: Visual consciousness is consciousness of a visual stimulus, as experienced through the visual sensory medium as a part of a process of seeing.

classes.label: auditory consciousness
classes.definition: Auditory consciousness is consciousness of an auditory stimulus, as a part of a conscious process of hearing.

classes.label: tactile consciousness
classes.definition: Tactile consciousness is consciousness that is experienced in the tactile sensory medium, through the sensory medium of touch and pressure sensation.

classes.label: direct consciousness
classes.definition: Direct consciousness is consciousness of phenomenal experience, it is the given experience in consciousness of (for example) sounds, tastes, emotions and bodily feelings.

classes.label: hearing
classes.definition:
Hearing (auditory perception) is a mental process that is
a) produced by a causal process involving sound waves from a part of the environment of the subject being absorbed by detectors in the ear, and
b) is experienced by the subject as being so caused, and
c) in which the relevant part of the environment is thereby represented to the subject

classes.label: affective representation
classes.definition: A cognitive representation sustained by an organsim about its own emotions.

classes.label: communication
classes.definition: A communication process is an interpersonal process that involves the transmission of information between two organisms.

classes.label: belief
classes.definition: A mental disposition to represent a proposition to be true.

classes.label: personal capability
classes.definition: A bodily disposition whose realization ordinarily brings benefits to an organism or group of organisms, where "ordinarily" means within a typical range or context.

classes.label: musical capability
classes.definition: A personal capability that is realised in an activity of producing or interpreting music.

classes.label: wanting
classes.definition: A mental process that involves thinking about a state of affairs that is not yet the case together with a desire for that state of affairs to come about.

classes.label: capability to play piano
classes.definition: A musical capability that is realised in the production of music using a piano.

classes.label: capability to play violin
classes.definition: A musical capability that is realised in the production of music using a violin.

classes.label: mental capability
classes.definition: A personal capability that includes mental processes in its realisation.

classes.label: capability to read
classes.definition: A linguistic capability that is realised by processes in which textual concretisations of linguistic expressions are processed and understood.

classes.label: linguistic capability
classes.definition: A mental capability that is realised in processes of communication involving language or in expressions of language.

classes.label: capability to understand language
classes.definition: A linguistic capability that is realised in processes in which well-formed expressions in a given language are understood.

classes.label: capability to speak
classes.definition: A linguistic capability that is realised in processes in which well-formed vocal expressions in a given language are produced.

classes.label: capability to read music
classes.definition: A musical capability that is the ability to interpret the musical instructions represented in a musical score.

classes.label: tasting
classes.definition:
Taste perception is a mental process which is
a) produced by a causal process involving xenobiotic molecules from a part of the environment of the subject binding with specialized sensory cells in the tongue and nasal cavity, and
b) is experienced by the subject as being so caused, and
c) in which the relevant part of the environment is thereby represented to the subject

classes.label: smelling
classes.definition:
Smelling (olfactory perception) is a mental process which is
a) produced by a causal process involving xenobiotic molecules from a part of the environment of the subject binding with specialized sensory cells in the nasal cavity, and
b) is experienced by the subject as being so caused, and
c) in which the relevant part of the environment is thereby represented to the subject

classes.label: touching
classes.definition:
Touching (tactile perception) is a mental process which is
a) produced by a causal process involving pressure on the organism’s skin from a part of the environment of the subject, and
b) is experienced by the subject as being so caused, and
c) in which the relevant part of the environment is thereby represented to the subject

classes.label: thinking with language
classes.definition: A cognitive process that involves the manipulation of mental language.

classes.label: attachment
classes.definition: Affectional tie that one person or animal forms between himself and another specific one, a tie that binds them together emotionally and endures over time.

classes.label: daydreaming
classes.definition: Short-term detachment from one's immediate surroundings, during which a person's contact with reality is blurred and partially substituted by a visionary fantasy, especially one of happy, pleasant thoughts, hopes or ambitions, imagined as coming to pass, and experienced while awake.

classes.label: vigilance
classes.definition:
The ability to maintain attention and alertness over prolonged periods of time.


http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vigilance_%28psychology%29

classes.label: orgasm
classes.definition:
Orgasm is the sudden discharge of accumulated sexual tension during the sexual response cycle, resulting in rhythmic muscular contractions in the pelvic region characterized by sexual pleasure.

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orgasm

classes.label: libido
classes.definition:
The psychic energy that drives individuals toward sensual pleasures of all types, especially sexual ones.


http://www.apa.org/research/action/glossary.aspx

classes.label: extraversion
classes.definition: A personality trait manifesting itself in individual behavioral characteristics that are perceived as positive, assertive, social, and outgoing.

classes.label: neuroticism
classes.definition: A personality trait manifesting itself in individual behavioral characteristics that are perceived as angry, anxious, depressed, unstable, and vulnerable.

classes.label: openness to experience
classes.definition: A personality trait manifesting itself in individual behavioral characteristics that are perceived as revealing, curiosity, an appreciation of novelty and variety of experiences and ideas, invention, and unpredictability.

classes.label: olfactory consciousness
classes.definition: Olfactory consciousness is consciousness of an olfactory stimulus (scent), as experienced through the olfactory sensory medium as a part of a process of smelling.

classes.label: consciousness of self
classes.definition: Consciousness of self is the higher order consciousness that reflexively includes the awareness that the organism that is the subject of the conscious experience exists.

classes.label: proprioception
classes.definition:
Proprioception is a mental process which is
a) produced by a causal process specialized internal sensory cells in, for example, skin, muscles and joints, and
b) by which their location and state of motion and/or balance are represented to the organism, and
c) which is experienced by the subject as being so caused

classes.label: nociception
classes.definition:
Nociception is a mental process which is
a) produced by a causal process specialized internal sensory cells in, for example, skin, muscles and joints, and
b) by which actual or immanent tissue damage are reported to the organism, and
c) which is experienced by the subject as being so caused

classes.label: a memory
classes.definition: A memory is a mental disposition that is realized in a process of remembering, i.e. a memory of X is a disposition realized in the process of remembering X.

classes.label: consciousness of time
classes.definition: The subjective experience of time as a coherent process inhabited by oneself as an embodied thinking being

classes.label: intentionality
classes.definition: Intentionality is the fundamental quality of conscious mental processes of always having content, of being directed towards, or about something.

classes.label: bodily quality
classes.definition: A bodily quality is a quality that inheres in some extended organism.

classes.label: mental quality
classes.definition: A mental quality is a bodily quality that inheres in those structures of the extended organism that are essential for mental functioning.

classes.label: intentional modality
classes.definition: A structural capacity that shapes how an object of intentionality is represented for the subject.

classes.label: consciousness of space
classes.definition: The subjective experience of the spatial surroundings one inhabits as an embodied entity.

classes.label: consciousness of the body
classes.definition: The subjective experience of being an embodied entity.

classes.label: intersubjectivity
classes.definition: The subjective experience of other beings as self-aware entities.

classes.label: time intentional modality
classes.definition: The intentional structural capacity to experience lived time.

classes.label: protention
classes.definition: The partial structure of time consciousness that relates to linking and projecting the content of immediate moments to future moments (e.g. how the path of a moving object is intuitively projected).

classes.label: retention
classes.definition: The partial structure of time consciousness that relates to retaining past events in memory and linking them to present events (e.g. how the individual tones in a melody is intuitively linked together to form a whole).

classes.label: mental imagery
classes.definition: A mental process that evokes the representation of the sensory characteristics of objects or events when these are not immediately present to the senses.

classes.label: spoken communication
written communication
classes.definition:
A written communication process is an interpersonal process that:
(a) involves as participant at least two organisms,
(b) one of whom produces a message in writing that is well-formed in a given language;
(c) the other of whom reads the message and understands it.

classes.label: linguistic communication
classes.definition: A linguistic communication process is a communication process in which the information that is communicated is encoded in language.

classes.label: gestural communication
classes.definition: A gestural communication process is a communication process in which information is transferred by means of physical movements.

classes.label: subliminal process
classes.definition: A mental process that involves neuronal activity in response to a sensory stimuli but which is not the subject of consciousness.

classes.label: non-linguistic communication
classes.definition: A communication process in which information is transmitted without being encoded in the meaning units of any language.

classes.label: sign-language communication
classes.definition: A linguistic communication in which the meaning units are encoded in a sign language.

classes.label: facial expression communication
classes.definition: A non-linguistic communication process that involves the transmission of information by one participant interpreting the facial expressions of another participant.

classes.label: higher order consciousness
classes.definition: Higher order consciousness is consciousness of one's own mental states, a self-reflexive consciousness of the experience of being conscious, of having mental processes ongoing.

classes.label: personality
classes.definition: A bodily disposition that is an aggregate of complex dispositions, endures over a period of years and is realised as emotion, belief, mood, motivational processes or behaviour.

classes.label: personality trait
classes.definition: A personality trait is an individual disposition or predisposition that forms part of an overall personality and is realized in repeated occurrences of a specific mental process type or behavioural profile.

classes.label: emotion process
classes.definition: An affective process that is a synchronized aggregate of constituent mental processes including an appraisal process, which is valenced, has an object, and gives rise to an action tendency.

classes.label: affective appraisal process
classes.definition: A mental process that gives rise to an appraisal.

classes.label: physiological process involved in an emotion
classes.definition: A bodily process that encompasses all the neurophysiological changes accompanying an emotion, which take place in the central nervous system (CNS), neuro-endocrine system (NES) and autonomous nervous system (ANS).

classes.label: emotional behavioural process
classes.definition: An emotional behavioural process is the behaviour of the organism in response to the appraisal, which includes the characteristic facial expressions for particular emotion types.

classes.label: affective appraisal
classes.definition: A cognitive representation of the emotional relevance of an object or event to the organism.

classes.label: subjective affective feeling
classes.definition: An affective process that involves the experience of internal or external sensory stimuli.

classes.label: emotional action tendency
classes.definition: A bodily disposition to behaviour that inheres in an organism by virtue of the physical changes brought about by an emotion process.

classes.label: anger
classes.definition: Anger is a negative emotion, characterised by feelings of unpleasantness and high arousal, in the form of antagonistic feelings and action tendencies. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: irritation
classes.definition: An unpleasant emotion closely related to anger but lower in intensity and without the moral dimension of blame and seriousness that is implicated in anger. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: annoyance
classes.definition: A negative emotion that is a mild form of anger.

classes.label: fury
classes.definition: An intensely negative emotion that is a very strong form of anger.

classes.label: rage
classes.definition: A negative emotion that is a strong form of anger.

classes.label: aggression
classes.definition: Any behaviour that is intended to harm another person who wants to avoid the harm. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: grief
classes.definition: Grief is an intense negative emotion following a bereavement, i.e. the loss of a significant person through that person's death. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: violence
classes.definition: Violence is aggression that has extreme physical harm as its goal. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: contempt
classes.definition: A negative emotion generally elicited by the negative evaluation of others and their actions. Usually elicited by violations of community codes. Closely related to anger and disgust. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: disgust
classes.definition: A negative emotion that is characterised by a need to get rid of, or distance oneself from, a stimulus that is appraised as repulsing.

classes.label: core disgust
classes.definition: Disgust elicited by "contaminated" food substances: rotten food, culturally variable "bad" food, certain animals associated with rotten food (maggots, rats), and every body product except tears. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: animal-nature disgust
