classes.definition: Disgust elicited by poor hygiene, inappropriate sex, gore or violations of bodily boundaries, and death or the odor of decay. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: interpersonal disgust
classes.definition: Disgust elicited by contact with others, especially contact with strangers or other individuals or groups we are averse to. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: moral disgust
classes.definition: Disgust elicited by some kinds of especially egregious moral violations. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: hate
classes.definition: A strong, negatively valenced emotion directed against a whole person for who or what they are. Often directed at whole groups based on religion, ethnicity, or race. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: jealousy
classes.definition: A negative emotion aroused when a person feels threatened by a rival in his or her relationship with another individual, in particular an intimate partner. Involves feelings of threat, fear, suspicion, distrust, anxiety, anger, betrayal, and rejection. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: fear
classes.definition: A negative emotion that is aversive and characterised by feelings of threat and impending doom, and by an urge to get out of the situation.

classes.label: terror
classes.definition: An extremely negative emotion that is an overwhelmingly strong fear.

classes.label: anxiety
classes.definition: A negative emotion that is aversive and provoked by the prospect of distal threat.

classes.label: stress (emotion)
classes.definition: A negative emotion in response to a stressful elicitor. May be acute or chronic.  Associated with health implications, such as impaired resistance to infectious diseases. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: despair
classes.definition: A negative, high intensity emotion characterised by loss of hope and loss of interest. Associated with action tendencies of harm to self or others. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: crying
classes.definition: A multimodal behaviour consisting of tears, non-verbal vocalisations (wails, sobs), and facial expressions of distress. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: surprise
classes.definition: An emotion caused by encountering unexpected events.

classes.label: interest
classes.definition: Interest is a positive emotion which motivates learning, exploration and curiosity. Feelings of interest are associated with the novelty and complexity of stimuli. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: joy
classes.definition: A pleasant, positive emotion which arises in safe and familiar circumstances, when people have made progress towards important personal goals, especially when the progress is better than expected. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: pleasure (emotion)
classes.definition: A positive emotion which is sought out and is associated with happiness and satisfaction.

classes.label: sensory pleasure
classes.definition: Pleasure in smell, touch, sight, sound and taste. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: mastery pleasure
classes.definition: Pleasure derived from mastery, including the experience of flow. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: social pleasure
classes.definition: Pleasure derived from social contact. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: sexual pleasure
classes.definition: Pleasure that is experienced as a result of sexual activities.

classes.label: pride
classes.definition: A positive emotion associated with the appraisal of one's positive social worth, a signal that one is likely to be socially accepted. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: happiness
classes.definition: A positive emotion which is experienced in reaction to a positive experience or event. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: serenity
classes.definition: An emotional state that is positively valenced, calm, peaceful and untroubled.

classes.label: amusement
classes.definition: A positive emotion that accompanies appraisal of an object, situation or event as humourous.

classes.label: elation
classes.definition: A very positive emotion accompanied by feelings of exhilaration.

classes.label: euphoria
classes.definition: An intensely positive emotion and strong feeling of excitement.

classes.label: contentment
classes.definition: A pleasant emotion, which can be defined as a milder form of joy. Associated with physical inactivity ('do nothing' action tendencies). [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: love
classes.definition: A strong emotion associated with feelings of desire, warmth and intimacy for another person. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: companionate love
classes.definition: Less intense, longer-lasting love which is characterised by affection, commitment, intimacy and a concern for the welfare of the loved one. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: passionate love
classes.definition: A powerful longing for union with the beloved, characterised by a confusion of feelings -- elation and pain, tenderness and sexuality, altruism and jealousy.

classes.label: disappointment
classes.definition: Disappointment is a negative emotion which is triggered by the disconfirmation of the prospect of a desirable event. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: compassion
classes.definition: An emotion evoked for a person who is in distress. The conditions for compassion involve perceiving the other as in need, and valuing the other's welfare. Associated with altruistic motivation. [Source: OCEAS]

classes.label: guilt
classes.definition: A negative self-evaluative emotion that occurs when a person brings about a negative outcome by acts of commission or omission that violate internal or external moral standards.

classes.label: shame
classes.definition: A negative emotion that is distressing and occurs when one appraises one's behaviour or circumstance as wrong, dishonourable, immodest or indecorous.

classes.label: sadness
classes.definition: A negative emotion felt when an event is appraised as unpleasant and resulting in loss or failure.

classes.label: appraisal of suddenness
classes.definition: An affective appraisal which represents an evaluation of how suddenly an event occurred.

classes.label: appraisal of familiarity
classes.definition: An affective appraisal that represents an evaluation of how familiar an object or event is.

classes.label: appraisal of predictability
classes.definition: An affective appraisal that represents an evaluation of how predictable an event was.

classes.label: appraisal of expectedness
classes.definition: An affective appraisal that represents an evaluation of whether an event was expected to occur.

classes.label: appraisal of pleasantness
classes.definition: An affective appraisal that represents an evaluation of the pleasantness of an object or event.

classes.label: appraisal as sudden
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that an event occurred suddenly.

classes.label: appraisal as not sudden
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that an event did not occur suddenly.

classes.label: appraisal as familiar
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that an object or event is familiar.

classes.label: appraisal as not familiar
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that an object or event is not familiar.

classes.label: appraisal as predictable
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that an event was easy to predict.

classes.label: appraisal as not predictable
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that an event was not easy to predict.

classes.label: appraisal as expected
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that an event was expected.

classes.label: appraisal as not expected
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that an event was not expected.

classes.label: appraisal as pleasant
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that an object or event is pleasant.

classes.label: appraisal as unpleasant
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that an object or event is unpleasant.

classes.label: appraisal of goal importance
classes.definition: An affective appraisal that represents an evaluation of whether an event or object is important to the person's goals or needs.

classes.label: evaluation as important to goals
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that the event or object is important to the person's goals or needs.

classes.label: evaluation as not important to goals
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that the event or object is not important to the person's goals or needs.

classes.label: appraisal of causal agency
classes.definition: An affective appraisal that represents an evaluation of who or what caused an event.

classes.label: appraisal as caused by self
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that an event was caused by oneself.

classes.label: appraisal as caused by chance
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that an event was caused by chance.

classes.label: appraisal as caused by an other
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that an event was caused by another person.

classes.label: feeling good
classes.definition: A subjective affective feeling that is positively valenced.

classes.label: feeling tired
classes.definition: A subjective affective feeling of a need for sleep.

classes.label: appraisal as caused supernaturally
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that an event was caused by a supernatural agent (God, the ancestors, ghosts...).

classes.label: appraisal of causal intent
classes.definition: An affective appraisal that represents an evaluation of the causal intent of the person who (is evaluated to have) caused an event.

classes.label: appraisal as deliberate
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that an event was deliberately (intentionally) caused.

classes.label: appraisal as unintended
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that an event was caused unintentionally.

classes.label: appraisal of desirability of consequences
classes.definition: An appraisal of desirability that represents an evaluation of the desirability of the expected consequences of an event.

classes.label: appraisal as desirable consequences
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that the expected consequences of an event are desirable.

classes.label: appraisal as undesirable consequences
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that the expected consequences of an event are undesirable.

classes.label: appraisal of urgency of response
classes.definition: An affective appraisal that represents an evaluation of the urgency of responding to an event.

classes.label: appraisal as urgent response
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that an event requires an urgent (immediate) response.

classes.label: appraisal as not urgent response
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that an event does not require an urgent response.

classes.label: appraisal of avoidability of consequences
classes.definition: An affective appraisal which represents a judgement about how avoidable the expected consequences of an event will be.

classes.label: appraisal as avoidable consequences
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents a judgement that the expected consequences of an event are in principle avoidable or modfiable.

classes.label: appraisal as unavoidable consequences
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents a judgement that the expected consequences of an event will be difficult to avoid or modify.

classes.label: appraisal of congruence with ideals
classes.definition: An affective appraisal which represents a judgement about whether an event is consistent with the person's standards or ideals.

classes.label: appraisal as congruent with ideals
classes.definition: An appraisal which represents a judgement that an event is consistent with the person's standards or ideals.

classes.label: appraisal as not congruent with ideals
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents a judgement that an event is inconsistent with a person's standards or ideals.

classes.label: appraisal of social attention
classes.definition: An affective appraisal which represents a judgement about the direction and nature of the social attention surrounding an event.

classes.label: appraisal as being at the centre of attention
classes.definition: An appraisal which represents a judgement that the person is at the centre of the surrounding social attention. (That is, that all other nearby persons are paying attention to him/her.)

classes.label: appraisal as not being at the centre of attention
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents a judgement that a person is not at the centre of the surrounding social attention.

classes.label: appraisal of justice of treatment
classes.definition: An affective appraisal which represents an evaluation of whether the person was treated justly or unjustly by another person.

classes.label: appraisal as just treatment
classes.definition: An appraisal which represents an evaluation that the person was treated justly by another person.

classes.label: appraisal as unjust treatment
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that the person was treated unjustly by another person. (Injustice.)

classes.label: appraisal of dangerousness
classes.definition: An affective appraisal which represents an evaluation of how threatening an object or situation is.

classes.label: appraisal as dangerous
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that an object or situation presents a threat to the person.

classes.label: appraisal as not dangerous
classes.definition: An appraisal that represents an evaluation that an object or situation does not present a threat to the person.

classes.label: appraisal of loss
classes.definition: An affective appraisal that represents a belief that something or someone that is important to the person has been lost to the person.

classes.label: feeling at ease
classes.definition: A subjective affective feeling of being at ease, comfortable, relaxed.

classes.label: feeling bad
classes.definition: A subjective affective feeling that is negatively valenced.

classes.label: feeling energetic
classes.definition: A subjective affective feeling of having lots of energy, being energetic.

classes.label: feeling in control
classes.definition: A subjective affective feeling that one is in control of oneself, that one is fully the agent of one's behavior.

classes.label: feeling restless
classes.definition: A subjective affective feeling of restlessness, a state of not being calm, of an agitation to do something.

classes.label: feeling exhausted
classes.definition: Feeling tired to an extremely strong degree.

classes.label: shivering
parent_labels: physiological process involved in an emotion

classes.label: feeling calm
classes.definition: A subjective affective feeling of being calm, being relaxed, being at peace.

classes.label: limb weakening
parent_labels: physiological process involved in an emotion

classes.label: feeling out of control
classes.definition: A subjective affective feeling of not being in control, not being able to gain agency of one's own behavior.

classes.label: becoming pale
parent_labels: physiological process involved in an emotion

classes.label: feeling strong
classes.definition: A subjective affective feeling of strength, capability, energy and capacity to do things.

classes.label: feeling weak
classes.definition: A subjective affective feeling of weakness, lack of energy and/or capability, faintness, absence of strength.

classes.label: experiencing a lump in the throat
parent_labels: physiological process involved in an emotion

classes.label: feeling alert
classes.definition: A subjective affective feeling of being wide awake, alert, having active attention and perception.

classes.label: experiencing discomfort in the stomach
parent_labels: physiological process involved in an emotion

classes.label: heart beating at slower rate
parent_labels: physiological process involved in an emotion

classes.label: feeling nervous
classes.definition: A subjective affective feeling of being not at ease or agitated.

classes.label: facial expression behaviour
classes.definition: A behavioural process that involves a change in the expression of the face.

classes.label: smiling
classes.definition: A facial expression behaviour in which the person smiles.

classes.label: jaw dropping
classes.definition: A facial expression behaviour in which the jaw drops.

classes.label: pressing lips together
classes.definition: A facial expression behaviour in which the lips are tightly pressed together.

classes.label: raising eyebrows
classes.definition: A facial expression behaviour in which the eyebrows are raised.

classes.label: frowning
classes.definition: A facial expression behaviour in which the person frowns.

classes.label: closing eyes
classes.definition: A facial expression behaviour in which the eyes are closed.

classes.label: opening eyes widely
classes.definition: A facial expression behaviour in which the eyes are opened widely.

classes.label: neutral expression
classes.definition: A facial expression behaviour which appears very neutral (showing no expression).

classes.label: moving abruptly
classes.definition: A bodily movement behaviour which involves abrupt movements.

classes.label: moving towards people
classes.definition: A bodily movement behaviour which involves moving, or leaning, towards people (approach).

classes.label: moving away from people
classes.definition: A bodily movement behaviour which involves moving, or leaning, away from people (avoidance).

classes.label: staying still
classes.definition: A bodily movement behaviour which involves remaining still.

classes.label: heart beating at faster rate
parent_labels: physiological process involved in an emotion

classes.label: muscles relaxing
parent_labels: physiological process involved in an emotion

classes.label: muscles becoming tense
parent_labels: physiological process involved in an emotion

classes.label: breathing at a more rapid rate
parent_labels: physiological process involved in an emotion

classes.label: breathing at a slower rate
parent_labels: physiological process involved in an emotion

classes.label: temperature rising (experienced as feeling warm)
parent_labels: physiological process involved in an emotion

classes.label: perspiring
parent_labels: physiological process involved in an emotion

classes.label: experiencing heat in cheeks or chest
experiencing warm sensation in whole body
blushing
parent_labels: physiological process involved in an emotion

classes.label: temperature falling (experienced as feeling cold)
parent_labels: physiological process involved in an emotion

classes.label: speaking loudly
classes.definition: Speaking with a voice louder than usual.

classes.label: speaking softly
classes.definition: Speaking with a voice softer than usual.

classes.label: speaking with trembling voice
classes.definition: Speaking with a voice that is hesitant or trembling.

classes.label: speaking assertively
classes.definition: Speaking with a voice that is confident and assertive.

classes.label: not speaking
classes.definition: Remaining silent, not producing spoken utterances.

classes.label: speaking a short utterance
classes.definition: Speaking behaviour in which a short utterance is produced.

classes.label: speaking a long utterance
classes.definition: Speaking behaviour in which a long utterance is produced.

classes.label: speaking with altered speech melody
classes.definition: Speaking with an altered rhythm or melody of speech relative to the norm for that person.

classes.label: speaking in a disturbed fashion
classes.definition: Speaking in a manner which is disturbed relative to what is the norm for that person.

classes.label: speaking at a faster rate
classes.definition: Speaking in a manner that is faster than the norm for that person.

classes.label: speaking at a slower rate
classes.definition: Speaking in a manner that is slower than the norm for that person.

classes.label: panic
classes.definition: A severe episode of fear with strong associated discomfort and thoughts of impending harm.

classes.label: boredom
classes.definition: A negative emotion that is the appraisal of one's current surroundings and activities as not interesting or stimulating.

classes.label: curiosity
classes.definition: A positive emotion that is an interest and engagement in an object or situation with a desire to know more.

classes.label: concern
classes.definition: A negative emotion that is a mild form of worry about a particular object or situation.

classes.label: satisfaction
classes.definition: Satisfaction is an emotion that is experienced when one's wishes, expectations or needs are fulfilled.

classes.label: dubious
classes.definition: A negative emotion accompanying uncertainty about a judgement or decision.

classes.label: worry
classes.definition: A negative emotion that is about a future or possible object or event that is appraised negatively.

classes.label: canonical angry facial expression
classes.definition: The canonical facial expression associated with the experience of anger.

classes.label: confusion
classes.definition: A negative emotion that is about a sense of uncertainty or bewilderment within oneself.

classes.label: canonical emotional facial expression
classes.definition: Characteristic facial expressions that are made when a person is undergoing a so-called "basic" emotions. These are canonical, that is, individual facial expressions when undergoing emotions can vary or not change at all. However, research indicates evidence for the existence of characteristic canonical facial expressions that are displayed when experiencing certain emotions even across cultures.

classes.label: expectant
classes.definition: A positive emotion that involves the anticipation that something desirable will occur.

classes.label: canonical fearful facial expression
classes.definition: The canonical facial expression associated with the experience of fear.

classes.label: hope
classes.definition: A positive emotion that is a longing for something to happen with an appraisal of its happening as both possible and positive.

classes.label: inspiration (emotion)
classes.definition: A positive emotion that is associated with a motivation and an idea to do or create something.

classes.label: schadenfreude
classes.definition: A complex emotion that consists of the experience of pleasure as caused by the misfortune of others.

classes.label: canonical happy facial expression
classes.definition: The canonical facial expression associated with the experience of happiness.

classes.label: canonical disgusted facial expression
classes.definition: The canonical facial expression associated with the experience of disgust.

classes.label: canonical sad facial expression
classes.definition: The canonical facial expression associated with the experience of sadness.

classes.label: canonical emotional voice utterances
classes.definition: The vocal utterances associated with the characteristic sound of an emotion. Obviously, any particular emotional instance may be associated with a great variety of different types of voice utterances or no voice utterances at all. However, "canonical" or characteristic voice utterances can be associated with core emotions.

classes.label: canonical angry voice utterance
classes.definition: Vocal utterances canonically associated with the experience of anger

classes.label: canonical fearful voice utterance
classes.definition: Vocal utterances canonically associated with the experience of fear

classes.label: canonical disgusted voice utterance
classes.definition: Voice utterances characteristically associated with the experience of disgust.

classes.label: canonical happy voice utterance
classes.definition: Voice utterance characteristically associated with the experience of happiness.

classes.label: canonical sad voice utterance
classes.definition: Voice utterance characteristically associated with the experience of sadness.

classes.label: canonical surprised voice utterance
classes.definition: Voice utterance canonically associated with the experience of surprise

classes.label: canonical surprised facial expression
classes.definition: Characteristic facial expression made when a person is undergoing an experience of surprise.

classes.label: appraisal as being disliked
classes.definition: An affective apraisal that represents a judgement that one is being disliked

classes.label: appraisal as being liked
classes.definition: An affective appraisal that represents a judgement that one is being liked

classes.label: mood process
classes.definition: A mood process is a mental process that involves affect (is valenced), and gives rise to a number of behavioural dispositions, but unlike an emotion has no object. Moods are usually longer-lived than emotion processes, but there are exceptions.

classes.label: valence
classes.definition: Valence is a process profile of an emotion, mood, or affective bodily feeling (such as pleasure and pain). Valence can be positive or negative, with different strengths in both directions. For example, pleasure is positively valenced while pain is negatively valenced.

classes.label: affective process
classes.definition: A mental process that has positive or negative valence.

classes.label: anxious mood
classes.definition: A mood process that is a generalised feeling of fearfulness and gives rise to a heightened disposition to experience anxiety, fear and other negatively valenced emotions.

classes.label: irritable mood
classes.definition: A mood process that is a general feeling of annoyance and gives rise to a heightened disposition to anger and other negatively valenced emotions.

classes.label: cheerful mood
classes.definition: A mood process that is is a general feeling of well-being and gives rise to a heightened disposition to happiness, amusement and other positively valenced emotions.

classes.label: emotion disposition
classes.definition: An emotion disposition is a disposition to repeated emotion process individuated by being of the same type and about the same object.

classes.label: enthusiasm
classes.definition: A positive emotion reflecting energy and passion for something.

classes.label: merry mood
classes.definition: A mood process that is a general feeling of enjoyment and festivity and gives rise to a heightened disposition to experience happiness, joy and other positively valenced emotions.

classes.label: feeling of pain
classes.definition:
A subjective affective feeling in an organism S, involving two integrated levels: 
(a) activation of the nociceptive system and associated emotion generating brain components of S, and 
(b) a simultaneous aversive sensory and emotional experience on the part of S, where (b) is phenomenologically similar to the sort of aversive experience involved in pain with concordant tissue damage.

classes.label: emotional personality trait
classes.definition: An emotional personality trait is a personality trait, a part of an overall personality, which predisposes the individual to repeated occurrences of a characteristic emotional process.

classes.label: feeling of hunger
classes.definition: A subjective affective feeling that involves discomfort and is associated with a need to consume food.

classes.label: feeling of thirst
classes.definition: A subjective affective feeling that involves discomfort and is associated with a need to consume water.

classes.label: positive valence
classes.definition: A valence that is pleasant, positive or good.

classes.label: negative valence
classes.definition: A valence that is negative, unpleasant or bad.

classes.label: positive surprise
classes.definition: Surprise with a positive valence

classes.label: negative surprise
classes.definition: Surprise with a negative valence.

classes.label: positive emotion
classes.definition: A positive emotion is an emotion that has a positive valence.

classes.label: negative emotion
classes.definition: A negative emotion is an emotion that has a negative valence.

classes.label: physical pleasure
classes.definition: A feeling good that is located in the body and is strongly positively valenced.

classes.label: gloomy mood
classes.definition: A mood process that is a general feeling of being down, having a negative outlook and gives rise to a heightened disposition to experience negatively valenced emotions.

classes.label: regret
classes.definition: A negative emotion that occurs when a person wishes they chose or acted differently in the past, due to the consequences of that choice or action being unfavourable.

classes.label: enjoyment
classes.definition: A positive emotion that is about an ongoing experience and reflects that the experience is being appraised as pleasurable.

classes.label: excited mood
classes.definition: A mood process that is a generalised feeling of enthusiasm, eagerness and energy, and gives rise to a heightened disposition to experience positively valenced emotions.

classes.label: feeling of desire
classes.definition: A subjective affective feeling that involves attraction to an imagined state of affairs.

classes.label: feeling of want
classes.definition: A feeling of desire that involves anticipated pleasure or satisfaction from an imagined state of affairs.

classes.label: feeling of need
classes.definition: A feeling of desire that involves anticipated relief from mental or physical discomfort.

classes.label: feeling of urge
classes.definition: A subjective affective feeling that involves a subjective experience of an impulse to engage in a behaviour.

classes.label: trust
classes.definition: A positive emotion characterized by assured reliance regarding the honesty, fairness, or abilities of an entity (e.g., person, object, or situation). This process involves an appraisal that the entity is reliable, safe, good and/or honest.

classes.label: mistrust
classes.definition: A negative emotion involving feelings of suspicion or doubt regarding the honesty, fairness, or abilities of an entity (e.g., person, object, or situation). This process includes an appraisal that the entity may be unreliable, potentially harmful and/or deceptive.

classes.label: appraisal of desirability
classes.definition: An affective appraisal of the extent to which something is good or beneficial.

classes.label: loneliness
classes.definition: A negative emotion arising from perceiving one’s social needs not being met by the quantity or quality of one’s social relationships.

classes.label: feeling lonely
classes.definition: A subjective affective feeling that is negatively valenced and arises from perceiving one’s social needs not being met by the quantity or quality of one’s social relationships.

classes.label: non-rapid eye movement sleep behavior
classes.definition: "Behavior related to all sleep stages in the circadian sleep/wake cycle other than REM sleep." [NBO:GVG]

classes.label: circadian rhythm
classes.definition: "Endogenously driven roughly 24-hour cycle in biochemical, physiological, or behavioral processes." [GOC:bf]

classes.label: circadian regulation of heart rate
classes.definition: "Any process in which an organism modulates its heart rate at different values with a regularity of approximately 24 hours." [GOC:rl]

classes.label: circadian regulation of systemic arterial blood pressure
classes.definition: "Any process in which an organism modulates its blood pressure at different values with a regularity of approximately 24 hours." [GO:GO\:0003052]

classes.label: circadian temperature homeostasis
classes.definition: "Any homeostatic process in which an organism modulates its internal body temperature at different values with a regularity of approximately 24 hours." [GOC:dbh]

classes.label: chase prey
classes.definition: Active pursuit of fleeing prey.

classes.label: flush prey
classes.definition: Behaviors in which predator forces potential prey to emerge from cover.

classes.label: construct capturing device
classes.definition: Building of a trap, web, net, or other structure to help ensnare potential food items.

classes.label: stalk prey
classes.definition: Approach to prey in manner designed to avoid early detection by prey.

classes.label: capturing behaviour
classes.definition: Suite of behaviors involved in securing a prey item once it has been located.

classes.label: capturing prey
classes.definition: Behaviors that result in ending flight of prey with successful predation.

classes.label: bodily process
classes.definition: A process in which at least one bodily component of an organsim participates.
